input: This executive summary presents a comprehensive overview of the delivery performance challenges currently facing the business, and sets out the recommendation that is presently under consideration for addressing them. That recommendation is to install the new scheduling system at Plant 2 first, while holding the other plants until Plant 2 results have been reported and reviewed in full. The scheduling programme is owned by the operations director, who will be responsible for its delivery. In terms of the underlying performance picture, on-time delivery over the last two quarters stood at 84%, which compares unfavourably with a target of 95%; these figures are drawn from a robust evidence base consisting of order records for 12 months covering no fewer than 11099 orders. By way of background, the business is a contract packaging firm operating 4 plants, generating revenue of $63 million per year. It is particularly notable that Plant 2 accounts for a disproportionate 54% of all late orders, which clearly indicates that the delivery shortfall is heavily concentrated at a single plant rather than being spread evenly across the wider business. Meanwhile, overtime cost reached $2.6 million last year, up a substantial 25% on the year before, and the order backlog currently stands at 3.9 weeks, compared with just 1.8 weeks a year ago, underscoring the scale of the deterioration. A scheduling system covering all plants has been quoted at $339k, whereas Plant 2 alone comes in at $151k, meaning that the first stage represents less than half of the full programme cost while testing the system precisely where late orders are concentrated. An internal estimate, rather than a vendor figure, suggests that the overtime reduction at Plant 2 could be in the region of 15–20% in the first year. Overall, the staged approach limits the initial commitment to the plant with the clearly measured problem, and allows the case for extending the system to the remaining plants to be built on actual reported results from Plant 2 rather than on estimates alone.
